content.output: Moving forward, policymakers and grid operators must address the structural risks posed by the unique load profiles of AI facilities, which include high-frequency oscillations that challenge frequency stability and voltage quality ([MDPI Energies](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/19/3/722)). Immediate action is required to accelerate transmission planning and enforce robust cost-allocation mechanisms that prevent the socialization of grid upgrade costs onto residential ratepayers, as seen in emerging state-level interventions like Virginia's HB503 ([Brookings Institution](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/confronting-and-addressing-rising-energy-bills-linked-to-data-centers/)). Without coordinated investment in generation diversity and transmission capacity, the U.S. grid faces a heightened risk of reliability failures and macroeconomic output losses that could far exceed the direct costs of electricity consumption ([Goldman Sachs](https://www.gspublishing.com/content/research/en/reports/2026/02/11/cefdda9f-3b7c-4a53-9950-dfcfa3c6bbc2.html)).
